text:
ella: hey team! first-day bootstrap almost done. running into two tiny wrinkles on WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04): git submodules failing with auth, and asdf ruby build errors. any quick tips?

samir: welcome! paste the errors if you can.

ella: submodule error when cloning private dotfiles: `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address`

ella: and asdf/ruby fails at compile: `error: missing header ruby.h` when running `asdf install ruby 3.1.2`

margo: submodule looks like git is trying HTTPS without credentials. Do you use the ssh remote in your dotfiles? `git remote -v` should show git@github.com:... not https://. If your org uses SSO+OIDC, we recommend SSH keys.

ella: my remote is https://. how do folks switch?

samir: easiest: `git config --global url."git@github.com:".insteadOf "https://github.com/"` then re-clone submodules. Or convert the remote in the repo: `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:org/repo.git`. We prefer the global insteadOf so CI behaves the same.

ella: switched to ssh and submodules started downloading but now ssh still prompts for passphrase every time. I'm using 1password for keys per onboarding doc.

margo: ensure ssh-agent is running and your key is loaded. On WSL, add to `~/.profile`: `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)" && ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa`. If you're using op (1Password CLI) we have this snippet in our dotfiles: `op item get "redwood/ssh-key" --fields label=privateKey | tr -d '\r' > ~/.ssh/id_rsa && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa && ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa`.

ella: I have op installed but `op signin` fails inside WSL due to a browser callback. Any workaround?

samir: yeah WSL browser flow can be annoying. Use `op signin --code` on the host mac/windows to get a short lived session token, then `export OP_SESSION_my=...` into WSL, or use `op signin --raw` on Windows and copy the token into WSL env. Docs have a note under Troubleshooting.

ella: thanks. after copying token, ssh keys loaded and submodules are good. now ruby: asdf ruby build fails on missing header.

margo: you need some dev packages: `sudo apt install build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libreadline-dev libyaml-dev libsqlite3-dev` and on WSL add `libgdbm-dev libncurses5-dev libffi-dev`. We also recommend `RUBY_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-readline-dir=$(brew --prefix readline)"` on mac; for WSL just install the listed packages.

ella: installed packages and re-ran asdf install and it's now compiling. one odd warning still: `warning: outdated openssl in /usr/local/opt/openssl`. Is that something to worry about?

samir: not for bootstrap. It means Homebrew (if you installed it) has an older openssl in your PATH. For WSL stick to distro openssl via apt or set `export PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH` temporarily during build. We'll update docs though.

ella: tiny follow-up: direnv won't let my `.envrc` run for the monorepo because it has `secret_vars` referencing a file in a sibling repo. Is there a safe pattern?

margo: prefer `source_env` patterns that read from `~/.config/redwood/envs/<project>` which devs populate locally. Then add that path to the org whitelist if it's shared. Avoid cross-repo `source_up` when it references private files.

ella: great — all green now. any pointers for a checklist link or someone to pair with for final steps?

ops-bot: Note: TICKET INF-5230 created to add WSL op signin guidance and git insteadOf trick to the onboarding checklist (assigned: infra-team).

infra-team: ping us in #eng-infra and we can do a 20-min pairing to finish dotfiles and ssh config.

ella: thanks everyone! appreciate the quick help :party:
